goal: The orchestrator claim store records each committed claim-lease transition (acquired, stolen, renewed, released, expired) as one immutable row in an append-only orchestrator_events ledger, written in the same transaction as the state change, readable as a global stream and a per-task timeline, on the in-memory and SQLite backends.

constraints: The event is INSERTed in the SAME store transaction as the task_claims mutation it describes (D-1): a committed acquire/steal/renew/release always has its event; a refused acquire (returns None), a stale renew (raises ClaimLostError), and a no-op release (deletes no row) each write NO event. The emit point is the store method, not the orchestrate loop.

Event taxonomy is exactly five types, one per committed task_claims insert/update/delete (D-2): acquired (fresh insert or a same-worker re-acquire), stolen (acquire over a DIFFERENT worker's lapsed lease), renewed, released (an actual row deletion), expired (one per claim reaped by sweep_expired_claims). stolen MUST be distinct from acquired so reclaim is observable.

Each event row carries: task_id, worker_id (the worker the event pertains to; for expired, the reaped holder), event type, the claim version after the transition, the lease expiry, the injected occurred-at timestamp (now), and a monotonic insertion id. occurred_at is the injected now, never a wall clock, so the ledger is deterministic and testable.

The ledger is append-only (D-2/criterion #9): N committed state changes on one task produce N events in insertion order, never deduped, upserted, or overwritten; re-acquiring after release appends a further acquired event. Provide a read API for the global stream (all events in id order) and a per-task timeline (one task's events in id order); provide NO method that updates or deletes an event.

Bump CURRENT_ORCH_SCHEMA_VERSION 3->4 additively (D-5): add orchestrator_events via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and converge the sentinel forward, mirroring the v2/v3 migration. A pre-existing v3 store (holding task_claims and work_items rows) opened by the new code MUST keep every row, open without OrchestratorSchemaError, and expose an empty orchestrator_events ledger (criterion #11) -- no drop-and-recreate.
InMemoryClaimStore must record events too (it is the test substrate and the operator-parity surface); its event store mirrors the durable backends' semantics.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do NOT add a 'lost' event on a failed renew -- a rejected renew changes no committed state, so there is nothing to attach an event to; the new holder's stolen event and the sweep's expired event capture reclaim (D-2).
Do NOT wire sweep_expired_claims into the orchestrate loop -- this task only proves the store emits expired events when sweep is invoked.
Do NOT add pruning, retention, rotation, or any growth cap; do NOT record source-sync events (those stay in source_syncs).
Do NOT alter acquire/renew/release/sweep/list return values, conflict-key refusal (00049), or optimistic-concurrency rejection.
Do NOT modify flywheel-core or the persistence-schema*.sql files; do NOT weaken or delete existing claim assertions under tests/.
Defer the Postgres backend to the dependent task -- this task delivers in-memory and SQLite only.
edge_cases: A acquires t (acquired); now advances past the lease; B acquires t -> a stolen event for B distinct from acquired, leaving the timeline [acquired(A), stolen(B)].
A acquires t; B steals t; A.renew_claim(stale) raises ClaimLostError and writes no event; A.release_claim(stale) deletes no row and writes no released event (timeline stays [acquired(A), stolen(B)]).
Two lapsed claims (A on t1, B on t2) plus one still-valid claim (C on t3): sweep writes exactly two expired events (t1/A, t2/B) and none for t3.
A refused acquire (live lease held by another worker, OR a conflict-key overlap) returns None and writes no event.
acquire -> renew -> renew -> release on one task yields exactly [acquired, renewed, renewed, released] in id order; a returned-constant or upserting ledger that collapses the two renews must fail.
